title: Common proper refinement of a finite valuation cover by quasi-modifications
statement: Let $X$ be a reduced quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme [def-pc-reduced-scheme], where quasi-compact means every open cover has a finite subcover and quasi-separated means intersections of quasi-compact opens are quasi-compact. Assume $X$ has finitely many irreducible components [def-weil-irreducible-components]. Let $Y_i\to X$ be finitely many integral birational quasi-modifications, and suppose that every centred valuation of every component of $X$ lifts to some $Y_i$. Then there is a reduced modification $p:X_1\to X$ and a finite open cover $X_1=\bigcup_i W_i$ with $X$-morphisms $W_i\to Y_i$ which are modifications. The index may be repeated after replacing the $Y_i$ by finite affine open covers. For an integral scheme $Y$ [def-pc-integral-scheme], its function field is the local ring at its generic point. A birational quasi-modification $Y\to Z$ is a separated finite-type morphism [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] identifying the function field of $Y$ with that of one irreducible component of the reduced scheme $Z$ [def-pc-reduced-scheme]. A centred valuation of that component means a valuation subring $W$ of its function field, together with a morphism $\operatorname{Spec}W\to Z$ inducing the generic-point map. It lifts to $Y$ when this morphism factors through $Y$. A modification is a proper morphism [def-weil-proper-morphism] inducing an isomorphism between schematically dense opens; an open immersion $j:U\hookrightarrow Z$ is schematically dense if $\mathcal O_Z\to j_*\mathcal O_U$ is injective. An $\eta$-modification is also an isomorphism on the whole generic fibre.

source.place: Proposition 3.2.6, Corollary 3.2.5 and Corollary 3.2.7, pp. 16--17; finite-component version obtained by applying them to the reduced component closures and taking a finite disjoint union; primary PDF read online, local archival copy WANTED (see report.md).

proof.text: If $X$ is empty, take $X_1$ empty with its empty cover. Otherwise give its finitely many irreducible components their reduced induced closed structures $C_a\hookrightarrow X$, using [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme]. Each $C_a$ is integral by [def-pc-integral-scheme], and is qcqs: it is closed in the qcqs scheme $X$, and on an affine chart its ring is a quotient. Assign $Y_i$ to the component containing the image of its generic point. Every point of $Y_i$ specializes that generic point, so its image is in $C_a$; [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-source-factors-through-closed-subscheme] gives a factorization $Y_i\to C_a\to X$. This factor is separated and of finite type: $Y_i\times_X C_a\cong Y_i$, so its diagonal is the same closed diagonal, and on affine charts its ring generators over the original base also generate over the quotient ring of $C_a$. The valuation-cover hypothesis holds over each $C_a$: a valuation morphism into $C_a$ is one into $X$, and any lift to a $Y_i$ has the same generic component and is over $C_a$, since $C_a\to X$ is a monomorphism. Taking the field $k(C_a)$ itself as a valuation ring shows that the family assigned to every component is nonempty.

source.place: Tags 01J3 (lemma-reduced-closed-subscheme), 0356 (lemma-map-into-reduction); finite-component reduction of Temkin Proposition 3.2.6

proof.text: Fix one component $C=C_a$, write $K=k(C)$, and use only the $Y_i$ assigned to it. By [sk-thm-nagata-compactification], each separated finite-type map $Y_i\to C$ has a dense compactification $Y_i\xrightarrow{j_i}\overline Y_i\to C$. Here the theorem applies because $C$ is qcqs. By [sk-def-nagata-sketch-data], $j_i$ is an open immersion and $\overline Y_i\to C$ is proper, with $\mathcal O_{\overline Y_i}\hookrightarrow j_{i*}\mathcal O_{Y_i}$. The latter injection kills nilpotents, since $Y_i$ is reduced. It also shows that every nonempty open of $\overline Y_i$ meets $Y_i$: otherwise its structure sheaf would be zero. Thus $Y_i$ is topologically dense, $\overline Y_i$ is irreducible, and $\overline Y_i$ is integral by [def-pc-integral-scheme]. Its generic point and function field are those of its nonempty open $Y_i$, hence the prescribed $K$.

source.place: Tag 0F41, theorem-nagata; density is the dense-compactification assertion of sk-thm-nagata-compactification

proof.text: The fibre of each $\overline Y_i$ over the generic point of $C$ is exactly $\operatorname{Spec}K$, with the specified generic map. Indeed choose a nonempty affine $\operatorname{Spec}A\subset C$. For any nonempty affine chart $\operatorname{Spec}B$ of its inverse image, [lem-sc-integral-function-field-affine-fraction] identifies $A$ and $B$ with subrings of $K$, compatibly with the structural map. Thus $A\subseteq B\subseteq K=\operatorname{Frac}(A)$ and $B\otimes_A K=K$: localization at the nonzero elements of $A$ already contains $\operatorname{Frac}(A)$ and remains a subring of $K$. By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] these are precisely the generic-fibre charts. They glue to one $\operatorname{Spec}K$, since every two nonempty opens of the integral $\overline Y_i$ contain its generic point and their identifications induce the identity on $K$. This is an affine localization computation, with no finiteness or Noetherian assumption on $A$.

Form the finite nonempty fibre product $P=\prod_C\overline Y_i$, using [def-pc-fibre-product]. Repeated proper base change and composition, [lem-weil-pbc-proper-base-change] and [lem-weil-pbc-proper-composition], show that $P\to C$ is proper. Step 3 gives $P_K=\operatorname{Spec}K$; denote its point by $\xi$. Let $Z\hookrightarrow P$ be the reduced induced closed subscheme on $\overline{\{\xi\}}$, which exists by [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme]. By [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-proper], the structural map $r:Z\to C$ is proper. We use this explicit reduced closure, rather than a whole fibre product with possible extra components.

source.place: Tags 01W3 (lemma-composition-proper), 01W4 (lemma-base-change-proper), 01W5 (lemma-closed-immersion-proper); Schemes 01J3 for the reduced closure

proof.text: The scheme $Z$ is nonempty, reduced and irreducible, hence integral by [def-pc-integral-scheme]. Its generic fibre is the full $\operatorname{Spec}K$: it is a closed subscheme of $P_K=\operatorname{Spec}K$ and contains $\xi$, so its defining ideal in the field $K$ is zero. In particular the residue field at $\xi$, and thus the function field of $Z$, is $K$. Every projection $q_i:Z\to\overline Y_i$ induces the identity on this specified $K$. These assertions use just the reduced closed structure from Step 4 and the calculation of the single generic fibre.

source.place: Tag 01J3, lemma-reduced-closed-subscheme; integral means reduced and irreducible, Properties Tag 01ON

proof.text: Since $Z\to C$ is proper and $\overline Y_i\to C$ is separated, [lem-weil-pbc-proper-to-separated] makes each projection $q_i:Z\to\overline Y_i$ proper. Put $W_i=q_i^{-1}(Y_i)=Z\times_{\overline Y_i}Y_i$. It is open in $Z$ by [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-base-change], and $h_i:W_i\to Y_i$ is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-base-change]. It contains $\xi$ because the generic point of $\overline Y_i$ belongs to $Y_i$. Hence $W_i$ is a nonempty integral open with function field $K$, and $h_i$ induces the identity of $K$ by Step 5 and [lem-sc-integral-function-field-affine-fraction]. All squares and maps here are over $C$, and therefore over $X$.

source.place: Tags 01W4 (lemma-base-change-proper), 01W6 (lemma-image-proper-scheme-closed), part (2); Schemes open-immersion base change

proof.text: For each of the maps $r:Z\to C$ and $h_i:W_i\to Y_i$, choose a nonempty affine target $V$ and a nonempty affine source chart $U$ inside its inverse image on which the map is of finite type. Such a chart exists by [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], since these maps are proper and dominant. Apply [lem-sbc-affine-birational-fraction-ring-equiv] with its affine base $S=V$, its $X=U$, its $Y=V$, and its two structural maps the restricted morphism and the identity. Both are locally of finite type; [lem-sc-integral-function-field-affine-fraction] identifies their fraction fields with the same $K$, and the isomorphism is the identity on every element of the base ring. The resulting $V$-isomorphism between dense opens of $U$ and $V$ is necessarily the restriction of the given map, because the second structural map is the identity. Those opens are also dense in the corresponding integral source and target. Thus $r$ and every $h_i$ induce isomorphisms between nonempty dense opens; no assertion about a normal target is needed.

source.place: Tag 0BAC, lemma-birational-birational, integral locally-finite-type case; specialized through the existing affine fraction-ring criterion

proof.text: Every nonempty open of an integral scheme is schematically dense. To verify the particular claim needed here, take an affine chart $\operatorname{Spec}A$ and a section whose restriction to the given dense open is zero. Its germ at the generic point is zero, and the injection $A\hookrightarrow k(Z)$ (or into the function field of the relevant integral scheme) in [lem-sc-integral-function-field-affine-fraction] makes that section zero. Affine charts test injectivity of the sheaf map. Consequently all dense opens in Step 7 are schematically dense. Combined with properness, this proves that $r$ and each $h_i$ are modifications in exactly the sense of the item. The remaining task is to prove that the opens $W_i$ cover $Z$.

source.place: Tag 01RV, lemma-integral-scheme-rational-functions; explicit verification of schematic density

proof.text: Take any $z\in Z$. On an affine neighbourhood $\operatorname{Spec}B$ of $z$, $B$ is a domain with fraction field $K$ by [lem-sc-integral-function-field-affine-fraction]. The local ring $\mathcal O_{Z,z}$ is a localization of $B$ by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization], so it too has fraction field $K$. By [lemma-nagata-local-domain-valuation-dominates] choose a valuation ring $V\subseteq K$ dominating $\mathcal O_{Z,z}$. Its local inclusion gives a morphism $v:\operatorname{Spec}V\to Z$ sending the closed point to $z$, by [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-from-spec-local-ring]. Its restriction to $\operatorname{Spec}K$ is the specified generic point, since the ring map is the inclusion in $K$. Thus $rv$ is one of the centred valuations of $C$ in the hypothesis.

By the hypothesis over $C$ verified in Step 1, $rv$ lifts to some $u:\operatorname{Spec}V\to Y_i$. Compare the two $C$-morphisms $q_i v$ and $j_i u$ from $\operatorname{Spec}V$ to $\overline Y_i$. They have the same restriction to $\operatorname{Spec}K$: Step 3 identifies the whole generic fibre with $\operatorname{Spec}K$ and its structural map with the identity. Since $\overline Y_i\to C$ is separated, [lemma-nagata-separated-valuation-lift-unique] gives $q_i v=j_i u$. At the closed point this says $q_i(z)\in Y_i$, so $z\in W_i$. As $z$ was arbitrary, the finite opens $W_i$ cover $Z$. In particular the cover is proved by comparing actual valuation morphisms, not just their images in $C$.

source.place: Tag 01L0, lemma-valuative-criterion-separatedness; valuation-cover argument underlying Temkin Corollaries 3.2.5 and 3.2.7

proof.text: Perform Steps 2--10 for each $C_a$, producing integral $Z_a$, proper $r_a:Z_a\to C_a$, and their finite covers by opens proper and birational over the assigned $Y_i$. Form $X_1=\coprod_a Z_a$ and the map $p:X_1\to X$ with restrictions $Z_a\to C_a\hookrightarrow X$, by [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family]. Each restriction is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-proper] and [lem-weil-pbc-proper-composition]. The finite coproduct map is proper directly from [def-weil-proper-morphism]: after any base change its closed images are finite unions of closed images; it is of finite type using the finite union of the affine covers for the component maps; and its diagonal on each open-and-closed $(a,b)$ block of $X_1\times_X X_1$ is the closed diagonal of $Z_a\to X$ when $a=b$ and the empty closed subscheme when $a\ne b$. The scheme $X_1$ is reduced, since all its open-and-closed pieces are integral. Their $W_i$ are opens of $X_1$ and cover it, with the same proper birational $X$-morphisms to the $Y_i$.

For each $a$, Step 7 supplies nonempty opens $A_a\subset Z_a$ and $B_a\subset C_a$ with $r_a:A_a\xrightarrow{\sim}B_a$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-dense-open-component-coproduct] to the component immersions and these $B_a$. Obtain a dense open $U\subset X$ such that $(\coprod C_a)|_U\to U$ is an isomorphism and $U\cap C_a\subset B_a$. The inverse images of $U\cap C_a$ in $A_a$ form an open $U_1\subset X_1$ isomorphic to $U$. Each is nonempty and dense in its integral $Z_a$, so $U_1$ is schematically dense by Step 8. To check schematic density of $U$ in the reduced $X$, pull a section zero on $U$ back to each $C_a$. It vanishes at its generic point, hence vanishes on $C_a$ by [lem-sc-integral-function-field-affine-fraction]. Its value in every residue field of $X$ is therefore zero, since the components cover $X$. The affine ideal formula of [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme], applied to the whole reduced scheme $X$, makes the section zero. This verifies injectivity of $\mathcal O_X\to j_*\mathcal O_U$. Together with Step 11, $p$ is a reduced modification, and all required claims now hold.

source.place: Tag 0BAJ, lemma-birational-isomorphism-over-dense-open, finite-component disjoint-open reduction; Schemes 01J3 ideal formula

proof.text: For the optional affine reindexing, each $Y_i$ is quasi-compact (finite type over qcqs $X$), so choose a finite affine open cover of it. A valuation morphism $\operatorname{Spec}V\to Y_i$ factors through any such affine containing the image of its closed point: its inverse image is open and contains the closed point of the local spectrum, hence all its points. Therefore these finitely many affine models still cover all centred valuations. Each is integral and separated of finite type over $X$: the affine open immersion is quasi-compact because $Y_i$ is quasi-separated, and finite generation is local on source. The construction of Steps 1--12 applies to this finite family and gives modifications to the selected affine opens. Relabel these opens by their original $i$, allowing repetitions as stated.
